generic_name: Insulin Syringe with Needle, 0.5 mL with Half-Unit Markings
purpose: This is a small syringe used to inject insulin for people managing diabetes. The 0.5 mL size is designed for lower insulin doses, and the half-unit markings allow you to measure your dose very precisely. It is not a medication itself, but a tool to deliver your insulin safely and accurately.
how_it_works: You draw insulin from your insulin vial into the syringe up to the dose your doctor prescribed. The half-unit markings on the barrel let you measure doses as small as half a unit, which is important for people who need very fine adjustments in their insulin. The thin needle is designed to make the injection as comfortable as possible under the skin.
common_side_effects: Since this is a syringe and not a medication, it does not cause drug side effects. However, you may notice minor skin irritation, small bruises, or slight pain at the injection site. Rotating your injection sites regularly helps prevent skin thickening or lumps.
warnings: Never share your syringe with anyone else, even family members — this can spread serious infections. Use each syringe only once and dispose of it safely in an approved sharps container. Keep syringes away from children. Make sure you are using the correct syringe size that matches your insulin concentration (usually U-100). Always double-check your dose before injecting.
typical_dosing: Use this syringe as directed by your doctor or diabetes care team. Draw up exactly the number of insulin units prescribed. The 0.5 mL syringe holds up to 50 units of U-100 insulin. The half-unit markings help you measure doses accurately. Ask your pharmacist or nurse to show you the proper injection technique if you are unsure.
